item.text:
**Orientation**
Abiy Ahmed had the formal executive authority of Ethiopia’s prime minister in 2023, but Ethiopia was not a nuclear-armed state and the nuclear chapter is mostly about restraint, treaty posture, and whether the government created or reduced catastrophic-risk exposure through war, coercion, and crisis management. The strongest 2023 evidence points to a conventional-security state under severe strain, not a government making nuclear-policy decisions.

The year’s material risk picture was driven by war and internal security, not nuclear escalation: the Tigray ceasefire remained partly implemented, while Amhara and Oromia saw renewed violence, emergency rule, arrests, and reported drone use. Information quality was weak in conflict areas because of connectivity blocks, intimidation of journalists, and restricted access.

**Developed Evidence**

1. **Ethiopia had no nuclear arsenal and remained within civilian nuclear-safety and safeguards frameworks**
- **Claim:** Ethiopia was not a nuclear-armed state in 2023; it had long-standing IAEA membership, a safeguards agreement tied to the NPT, and CTBT ratification. This matters because it sets the baseline for the chapter: Abiy was not managing an indigenous nuclear deterrent or nuclear command system.
- **Best source:** [IAEA country factsheet for Ethiopia](https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=ET) and [CTBTO press release on Ethiopia’s CTBT ratification](https://www.ctbto.org/resources/for-the-media/press-releases/ethiopia-ratifies-comprehensive-nuclear-test-ban-treaty)
- **Locator:** IAEA lines 3-5, 115-124; CTBTO lines 227-230.
- **Period fit:** Inherited baseline, active in 2023.
- **Ruler attribution:** Contextual only; this is state posture, not a personal decision record.
- **Contrary evidence:** None found in the inspected material suggesting a weapons program or nuclear armament.
- **Cautions:** This establishes non-nuclear status and treaty posture, not the absence of all radiological or dual-use risks.
- **Independent support:** [UN Treaty Collection NPT ratification record](https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showActionDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=0800000280120c21) and CTBTO’s signatory/ratification status page.

2. **Ethiopia’s formal nuclear obligations were limited to safeguards and test-ban commitments, not active weapons policy**
- **Claim:** Ethiopia had ratified the NPT in 1970 and ratified the CTBT in 2006; the IAEA record shows a safeguards agreement and additional protocol signature, but not a weapons program. This matters because it is the formal legal baseline for nuclear-risk responsibility.
- **Best source:** [UN Treaty Collection, NPT ratification action](https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showActionDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=0800000280120c21) and [IAEA Ethiopia country factsheet](https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=ET)
- **Locator:** UNTC lines 10-21; IAEA lines 115-124.
- **Period fit:** Inherited baseline relevant to 2023.
- **Ruler attribution:** Low to moderate; treaty posture is state-level and long-running.
- **Contrary evidence:** None located.
- **Cautions:** A treaty signature or ratification does not by itself prove compliance quality, but it does show Ethiopia was not operating outside the nuclear-normative framework.
- **Independent support:** CTBTO ratification notice and IAEA safeguards listing.

3. **No evidence of nuclear brinkmanship or nuclear-specific rhetoric by Abiy in the inspected 2023 material**
- **Claim:** In the 2023 sources inspected for this chapter, Abiy’s rhetoric centered on peace talks, internal security, and national unity; I found no credible evidence of nuclear threats, nuclear coercive signaling, or a nuclear doctrine shift. This matters because the lens asks whether he used nuclear language or posture irresponsibly.
- **Best source:** [FDRE PM Office “Our Government”](https://www.pmo.gov.et/government/) and [Reuters on the Amhara emergency](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ethiopia-declares-state-of-emergency-following-militia-clashes-3144776)
- **Locator:** PMO lines 21-25, 30, 45-47; Reuters headline and opening paragraph.
- **Period fit:** Target period.
- **Ruler attribution:** Direct for the public narrative; negative finding is based on the inspected source set.
- **Contrary evidence:** None found in the searched 2023 material.
- **Cautions:** This is an evidentiary absence, not proof that no such rhetoric existed elsewhere.
- **Independent support:** CTBT/IAEA posture also fits a non-nuclear rhetoric baseline.

4. **The 2022 Tigray cessation-of-hostilities process remained the main risk-reducing conflict framework in 2023**
- **Claim:** The AU said the cessation-of-hostilities agreement was intended to stop hostilities, restore humanitarian access and services, and support reconciliation, and later described implementation as steady. This matters because it is the clearest 2023 example of de-escalation linked to Abiy’s government.
- **Best source:** [African Union PAPS agreement page](https://www.aupaps.org/en/article/cessation-of-hostilities-agreement-between-the-government-of-the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-and-the-tigray-peoples-liberation-front-tplf)
- **Locator:** lines 70-84.
- **Period fit:** Directly concerns 2023 implementation of an inherited peace process.
- **Ruler attribution:** Strong, though shared with Tigrayan authorities and AU mediators.
- **Contrary evidence:** HRW and UN reporting say serious abuses and unresolved issues continued in Tigray despite the deal.
- **Cautions:** AU language is diplomatic and tends to emphasize success.
- **Independent support:** [HRW World Report 2024: Ethiopia](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia) and [UN Geneva briefing summary](https://www.unognewsroom.org/story/en/2217/un-human-rights-briefing-by-liz-throssell-on-ethiopia-report/6697).

5. **Amhara violence and the emergency response increased catastrophic-risk exposure**
- **Claim:** In August 2023, fighting between federal forces and Fano in Amhara escalated into a six-month state of emergency with arrest, curfew, gathering, and search powers. This matters because it shows severe state fragility and emergency coercion rather than durable risk reduction.
- **Best source:** [Reuters, Aug. 4, 2023](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ethiopia-declares-state-of-emergency-following-militia-clashes-3144776)
- **Locator:** opening paragraph and headline; [HRW’s 2024 country chapter](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia) lines 72-74.
- **Period fit:** Directly 2023.
- **Ruler attribution:** Strong.
- **Contrary evidence:** The government portrayed the measure as necessary to restore order; Amhara officials requested federal help.
- **Cautions:** Access to the region was constrained, so casualty and abuse estimates were incomplete.
- **Independent support:** HRW and UN reporting.

6. **The state of emergency was accompanied by arrests and communications restrictions**
- **Claim:** Amnesty reported that the government blocked major social media platforms from February 2023, and later reporting documented media restrictions, arrests, and detention tied to the Amhara emergency. This matters because the information clampdown reduced outside scrutiny during a high-risk security crisis.
- **Best source:** [Amnesty International, Mar. 9, 2023](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/03/ethiopians-in-social-media-blackout-for-second-month/) and [Freedom House Freedom on the Net 2023](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-net/2023)
- **Locator:** Amnesty lines 57-73; Freedom House lines 31-41.
- **Period fit:** Directly 2023.
- **Ruler attribution:** Strong.
- **Contrary evidence:** Government explanations cited public-order concerns and Orthodox Church tensions.
- **Cautions:** Rights groups are advocacy-oriented, but their claims are mutually reinforcing and consistent with other reports.
- **Independent support:** HRW lines 85-87, and Amnesty UK’s August 2023 Amhara statement.

7. **The 2023 security environment remained highly lethal, including reported government drone use**
- **Claim:** A UN human-rights briefing summary said at least 1,351 civilians were killed in Ethiopia in 2023 and that government UAV use caused 248 civilian deaths between Aug. 4 and Dec. 31, 2023. This matters because it is direct evidence that state force in 2023 was itself a major source of catastrophic harm.
- **Best source:** [UN Geneva multimedia newsroom summary of Ethiopia report](https://www.unognewsroom.org/story/en/2217/un-human-rights-briefing-by-liz-throssell-on-ethiopia-report/6697)
- **Locator:** summary text in the search result; the page itself was not fully accessible in the browser, so this is a high-confidence secondary citation only.
- **Period fit:** Directly 2023.
- **Ruler attribution:** Strong, because the summary attributes the UAV use to government forces.
- **Contrary evidence:** None in the inspected material that negates the specific casualty figure.
- **Cautions:** This is a briefing summary of a UN update, not the full report text.
- **Independent support:** HRW’s 2024 chapter reports severe fighting and mass arrests in Amhara; Reuters reported the emergency powers.

8. **Economic and humanitarian strain were severe, but they were not nuclear-policy outcomes**
- **Claim:** The World Bank said Ethiopia’s 2023 debt default, double-digit inflation, and food-aid dependence reflected multiple crises, including the Tigray conflict and droughts. This matters because it explains why existential-risk capacity was weak even absent nuclear issues.
- **Best source:** [World Bank Ethiopia overview](https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/country/ethiopia)
- **Locator:** lines 155-156.
- **Period fit:** Directly 2023, with inherited drivers.
- **Ruler attribution:** Moderate; the problems are partly inherited and partly policy-linked.
- **Contrary evidence:** None that changes the macro picture in the inspected set.
- **Cautions:** This is a broad country overview, not a ruler-only audit.
- **Independent support:** WHO’s 2023 public-health and food-insecurity reporting.

9. **Civilian nuclear-risk institutions existed, but they were about radiation control, not strategic weapons**
- **Claim:** IAEA records show Ethiopia’s nuclear-related institutional footprint was civilian: safeguards, radiation protection, and technical cooperation. This matters because it confirms the chapter should not treat Ethiopia as a strategic nuclear actor.
- **Best source:** [IAEA Ethiopia factsheet](https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=ET)
- **Locator:** lines 3-5, 83-124.
- **Period fit:** Baseline/inherited.
- **Ruler attribution:** Low.
- **Contrary evidence:** None found.
- **Cautions:** The record says little about actual staffing quality or 2023 policy priorities.
- **Independent support:** CTBTO and UNTC treaty records.

**Later retrospective evidence**
- **HRW 2024:** Confirms Amhara remained a major security disaster in 2023 and that emergency powers were used broadly.
- **UN Geneva summary:** Adds the most explicit civilian-casualty figure set for 2023 and attributes 248 civilian deaths to government UAV use.
- **World Bank overview:** Confirms the economic collapse and food-aid dependence.

**Information Environment**
- The most reliable 2023 evidence is about treaty status and conflict aftermath, not nuclear governance.
- Ethiopia’s information environment was poor: platform blocks, internet restrictions, detentions of journalists, and blocked access to conflict zones.
- The strongest limitation for this chapter is negative evidence: there is little sign of any substantive nuclear-policy agenda to evaluate in 2023.
- That absence itself is meaningful. It suggests the right analytic frame is “non-nuclear state with severe conventional security failures,” not “leader managing a nuclear deterrent.”

**Research Questions**
- Did Ethiopia maintain its safeguards and CTBT obligations cleanly in 2023, or were there any compliance issues not visible in the open record?
- Did any government body consider dual-use biological, cyber, or AI catastrophe-risk safeguards in 2023?
- How much of the 2023 civilian harm in Amhara came from federal force versus non-state actors?
- Did the Tigray ceasefire materially reduce existential-risk exposure, or just shift it geographically?
- Were there hidden procurement or security decisions affecting hazardous infrastructure, airpower, or command-and-control?

**Source Groups**

**Accepted / developed**
- [FDRE PM Office](https://www.pmo.gov.et/government/)
- [AU PAPS cessation agreement page](https://www.aupaps.org/en/article/cessation-of-hostilities-agreement-between-the-government-of-the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-and-the-tigray-peoples-liberation-front-tplf)
- [Amnesty International, Mar. 9, 2023](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/03/ethiopians-in-social-media-blackout-for-second-month/)
- [Freedom House: Ethiopia Freedom on the Net 2023](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-net/2023)
- [Reuters on Amhara state of emergency](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ethiopia-declares-state-of-emergency-following-militia-clashes-3144776)
- [HRW World Report 2024: Ethiopia](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia)
- [World Bank Ethiopia overview](https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/country/ethiopia)
- [IAEA Ethiopia factsheet](https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=ET)
- [CTBTO Ethiopia CTBT ratification](https://www.ctbto.org/resources/for-the-media/press-releases/ethiopia-ratifies-comprehensive-nuclear-test-ban-treaty)
- [UN Treaty Collection NPT record](https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showActionDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=0800000280120c21)
- [Transparency International Ethiopia profile](https://knowledgehub.transparency.org/country/ethiopia)
- [WHO Ethiopia cholera response](https://www.afro.who.int/countries/ethiopia/news/who-ethiopia-rapidly-scales-response-contain-cholera-outbreak-snpp-region)

**Corroboration only**
- [Reuters on OLA talks ending without deal](https://www.yahoo.com/news/ethiopia-says-talks-rebel-group-183509182.html)
- [Reuters on first round OLA talks](https://www.yahoo.com/news/first-round-peace-talks-between-143906076.html)
- [WHO 2023 public-health situation analysis](https://www.afro.who.int/countries/ethiopia/news/northern-ethiopia-public-health-situation-analysis-phsa-25-august-2023)
- [WHO on escalating public health needs, Dec. 2023](https://www.afro.who.int/countries/ethiopia/news/who-expresses-concern-escalating-public-health-needs-ethiopia)

**Uninspected leads**
- Full OHCHR report behind the UN Geneva summary.
- Ethiopian legal text for the August 2023 state of emergency.
- Any 2023 defense, aviation, or procurement material relevant to hazardous force posture.
- Any 2023 cyber, biosecurity, or AI-risk governance materials.

**Source Counts**
- Inspected sources: 12+.
- Developed evidence records: 9.
- Clear 2023 nuclear-specific policy actions found: 0.
- Clear 2023 nuclear-specific rhetoric incidents found: 0.
- Main gap: no substantive nuclear-risk policymaking appears in the open 2023 record; the relevant action is the absence of such a portfolio, alongside severe conventional-security failures.
